newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar profit-taking.

text.p: The won closed higher on Friday on dollar profit-taking, dealers said.
"The greenback is and will be in a consolidation phase for a while. But the 890-won level will be supported," said a foreign bank dealer.
The won ended at 892.70 against Thursday's close of 894.70, after staying in a 895.60-891.50 on a tug-of-war between dollar longs and shorts.
"Shorts won the battle today," said a local bank dealer. "The dollar is unlikely to go beyond the 900-won level while corporate selling orders await at around 896.00 mark."
Dealers said importer deals next week, estimated at $400-$500 million, would help the dollar.
"But the dollar demand is unlikely to be big as many companies hold enough dollars to settle their import accounts," said the domestic bank dealer.
The Bank of Korea said on Friday the country's current account deficit could exceed its 1997 forecast of $18 billion but dealers said the news did not have major impact on the maket.
Monday's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at between 893.00 and 893.30 against 895.40 today.
